## Description

This vignette reports the results of a longer perturbation analyses (*not* that ran in the previous vignette). This was built on the same vital rate models as in [Single VR Model](DIPM-020_Vital_rate_models.html), but where the IPM was run with limits from -200 to +200, with increments of 0.2 m (`n. bins = 2000`), and for 12 months. This perturbation is time consuming (~ 4h) to be rendered as a vignette efficiently. I will here load the results of the perturbation analyses stored in the folder `results_tokeep`.

## Setup

Loading data, packages, and models.

```{r}
# packages
library(whereipm)
library(tidyverse)


# IPM models
phasesIPMs <- readRDS(file.path(here::here(), "results_tokeep",
                                "K2000x12_lambda1_20190509",
                                "phaseModelsIPMs_K2000x12_lamb1_0509.rds"))
perturbationResults <- readRDS(file.path(here::here(), "results_tokeep",
                                         "K2000x12_lambda1_20190509",
                                       "perturbation_result_phase_models_K2000x12_lamb1_0509.rds"))
# extracting output list
outputs <- rownames(perturbationResults)

# colors
Cols <- wesanderson::wes_palette("Darjeeling1", 3, type = "discrete")
```

## Plotting

### IPM results

```{r}
# Early phase
plotly::plot_ly(x=1:ncol(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[1]]$pop.size), 
                y=rev(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[1]]$kernel.params$y), 
                z=phasesIPMs$IPMs[[1]]$pop.size, 
                type="contour")
# Mid phase
plotly::plot_ly(x=1:ncol(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[2]]$pop.size), 
                y=rev(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[2]]$kernel.params$y), 
                z=phasesIPMs$IPMs[[2]]$pop.size, 
                type="contour")
# Late phase
plotly::plot_ly(x=1:ncol(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[3]]$pop.size), 
                y=rev(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[3]]$kernel.params$y), 
                z=phasesIPMs$IPMs[[3]]$pop.size, 
                type="contour")


quick.plot(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[1]], "Init")
quick.plot(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[2]], "Middle")
quick.plot(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[3]], "End")
```

### Comparing output variables

I am here plotting the output variables from the three IPMs.

First, we can compare the entire progress of the invasion among the different phases.

```{r}
# extracting and storing IPM info
phasesIPMs <- phasesIPMs %>%
  mutate(front = map(IPMs, function(x){x[["front"]]}),
         speed = map(IPMs, function(x){c(x[["speed_front"]], NA)}),
         lambda = map(IPMs, function(x){c(x[["lambdas"]], NA)}))

toplot <- data.frame(phase = rep(unlist(phasesIPMs$phase),
                                 each = phasesIPMs$IPMs[[1]]$n.iterations+1),
                     time = as.factor(1:(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[1]]$n.iterations+1) - 1),
                     front = unlist(phasesIPMs$front),
                     speed = unlist(phasesIPMs$speed),
                     lambda = unlist(phasesIPMs$lambda)) %>%
  mutate(phase = factor(phase, levels = c("early", "mid", "late")))

f <- ggplot(toplot, aes(x = time, y = front, group = phase)) +
  geom_line(aes(col = phase)) + 
  ggtitle("Front advance") + ylab("front position (m)") + 
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = Cols)

s <- ggplot(toplot, aes(x = time, y = speed, group = phase)) +
  geom_line(aes(col = phase)) + 
  ggtitle("Speed of the front") + ylab("speed (m/month)") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = Cols)

l <- ggplot(toplot, aes(x = time, y = lambda, group = phase)) +
  geom_line(aes(col = phase)) + 
  ggtitle("Population growth rate") + ylab(expression(lambda)) +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.94,0.5), legend.title=element_blank()) +
  scale_color_manual(values = Cols)

png(file.path(here::here(), "results", "Figure1.png"), width = 8, height = 7, unit = "in", res = 200)
gridExtra::grid.arrange(f, s, l, ncol =1)
dev.off()
```


```{r, fig.height=8}
# obtaining the original values for output variables:
phasesIPMs <- phasesIPMs %>%
  mutate(
    orig.output =   map(IPMs, function(x){
      outs <- lapply(outputs, function(i){x[[i]]})
      names(outs) = outputs
      return(outs)
      }
      ))

# extracting original parameters and readying them for plotting
orig_outputs <- phasesIPMs %>%
  select(orig.output) %>%
  pull() %>%
  unlist() %>%
  matrix(ncol = nrow(phasesIPMs), nrow = length(outputs)) %>%
  t() %>%
  as.data.frame()
colnames(orig_outputs) <- outputs
# adding column defining phase and reshaping to long
orig_outputs <- orig_outputs %>%
  add_column(phase = unlist(phasesIPMs$phase)) %>%
  mutate(phase = factor(phase, levels = c("early", "mid", "late"))) %>%
  gather(key = "output", value = "value", -phase)

# checking
orig_outputs

# plotting selected outputs
plot_IPM_outputs(orig_outputs, which_to_show = outputs, y_spacing = 10, n_cols = 4)

# saving plot
selected <- c("final_front_position", "initial_front_speed", "final_front_speed",
              "avg_front_speed", "acceleration_est_front", "final_max_density")

pdf(file = file.path(here::here(), "results", "Outputs.pdf"), width = 6, height = 5)
plot_IPM_outputs(orig_outputs, which_to_show = selected, y_spacing = 10, n_cols = 3)
dev.off()
```

### Plotting perturbation results

Here, I am not running the perturbation analyses (too time consuming), but rather loading a stored perturbation result.

First, loading the perturbation results and rearranging the format to make it easier to plot.

**NOTE**: reproduction probability is here to be interpreted as the opposite of it. It is coded as the probability to *not* reproduce. So what appears to be a negative effect is actually a positive effect on the probability to have any offspring.

```{r}
# For ease of plotting, handling the array t make it a single data.frame with outputs for columns and parameters for rows

# first, though, reproduction probability is upside down, since here we're modelling the
# probability to NOT produce any offspring. I'll flip it for convenience.

perturbationResults[,'r.int',] = - perturbationResults[,'r.int',]

pResults <- aperm(perturbationResults, perm = c(2,1,3))
pResults <- data.frame(apply(pResults, 2, c),
                       expand.grid(dimnames(perturbationResults)[c(2,3)]))
colnames(pResults)[(ncol(pResults)-1):ncol(pResults)] <- c("params", "phase")

# reproduction probability is upside down, since here we're modelling the probability 
# to NOT produce any offspring. I'll flip it for convenience.


# creating a vector of better names for parameteres
paramnames <- c('survival (int)', 'survival (slo)',
            'repr p (int)',  'repr p (slo)',
            'offspr n (int)',  'offspr n (slo)',
            'ad dispersal (int)','ad dispersal (slo)',
            'ad distance (mean)', 'ad distance (sd)',
            'nat dispersal (int)','nat dispersal (slo)',
            'nat dispersal (landsc)', 'nat dispersal (loc x land)',
            'nat distance (mean)', 'nat distance (sd)')

## plotting all outputs
for(i in outputs){
  p <- ggplot(data = pResults, aes_string(x = "params", y = i, fill = "phase")) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.8, position = position_dodge()) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = Cols) +
    coord_flip()
  theme_minimal()
print(p + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = paramnames) +
  ggtitle(as.character(i)))
}

## saving key outputs in a single figure
pResults_long <- pResults %>%
  select(final_front_position, avg_front_speed, acceleration_est_front, 
         params, phase) %>%
  gather(key = "output", value = "p_change", -c(params, phase)) %>%
  mutate(output = str_replace_all(output, c("final_front_position" = "front position",
                           "avg_front_speed" = "speed (avg)",
                           "acceleration_est_front" = "acceleration")),
         output = factor(output, levels = c("front position", "speed (avg)", "acceleration", "max local density")),
         params = factor(params, levels = rev(unique(pResults$params))))

png(file = file.path(here::here(), "results", "Figure2.png"), width = 9, height = 4, unit = "in", res = 200)
ggplot(data = pResults_long, aes_string(x = "params", y = "p_change", fill = "phase"))+
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.7, position = position_dodge()) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = Cols) +
  ylab("proportional change") + xlab("modified parameter") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0), 
        axis.text = element_text(size = rel(0.6)), 
        strip.text.x = element_text(size = rel(1.3)), 
        panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = rgb(0,0,0,.2), size = 0.2),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank() ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, size = 0.2, colour = rgb(0,0,0,.2)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = rev(paramnames)) +
  facet_grid( ~ output)
dev.off()
```

Here, I re-run the linear models used to estimate acceleration.

```{r}
t <- 1:(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[1]]$n.iterations)

# early phase
early.front <- phasesIPMs$IPMs[[1]]$front[-1]
summary(lm(early.front ~ t + I(t^2)))

# mid phase
mid.front <- phasesIPMs$IPMs[[2]]$front[-1]
summary(lm(mid.front ~ t + I(t^2)))

# late phase
late.front <- phasesIPMs$IPMs[[3]]$front[-1]
summary(lm(late.front ~ t + I(t^2)))
```
